assumptions: Exact Python bool and str inputs from the admitted classifier projection.
The independently enumerated decision table expresses the intended versioned policy.
Python runtime and recorded source identities are trusted.
boundary: arithmetic_handoff.select only; the ontology reasoner, IO shell, native arithmetic and Schema2 refinement are separate obligations.
claim: The actual finite selection function agrees with the independent requirement-selection table throughout its declared input domain.

limitations: Finite selector only, not the ontology reasoner or Python interpreter correctness.
Native and Verus results are separately retained in qualification.json; they are not inferred from this table check.

conclusion: For every declared case, select(case) equals the independent table; bound requires complete consistent classification, a present individual, width, exactly one signedness, no unsupported requirement, and the matching target.
falsifiers: Any declared case with different production and oracle results
Any bound result with missing, incomplete, inconsistent or unsupported inputs
Any bound result selecting I256 for unsigned requirements or U256 for signed requirements

acceptance_tests: All 2304 cases compare equal and every bound case satisfies the explicit invariant.
deliverables: The bound source pair and retained successful test output.
lanes.goal: Exhaustively compare the actual finite selector to the independent table.

nonclaims: Full proof of Python ontology inference or source-binding IO

artifacts.role: independent finite table and exhaustive acceptance test

claim_mapping.claim_clause: Independent table plus exhaustive 2304-case enumeration and explicit bound invariants.
Actual implementation evaluated for each enumerated case.

quantifiers: All 2304 combinations: four closure statuses, two completeness flags, three consistency states, five independent boolean projections, and U256/I256/one representative unsupported target.
The five projections are individual presence, width, unsigned requirement, signed requirement, and unsupported requirement.
Unsupported target names form one equivalence class because production and oracle branch only on membership in the two supported names.

refinement.relation: Pointwise equality to the independent table on the declared finite domain; signedness preservation is a necessary condition of bound.
refinement.source_semantics: Admitted closure flags and explicitly projected requirement predicates.
refinement.target_semantics: A conditional bound target or a non-authoritative diagnostic state.
